Two scheduled rows carry the assistant's work on its own library: **26 stages**, of which 7 call a model. Capture runs in minutes; consolidation runs once a night, and its cron is the only thing ordering any of them. Everything else that runs unasked — including the upkeep of the machine itself — is on the [What runs on its own](/reference/what-runs/) page.

> These are the **shipped defaults**. Every value here lives in a config
> file you own once TESSERACT is installed, so your copy may differ — and
> should, once you tune it.


## `capture` — every 5 minutes

Deterministic, and it never calls a model. What you say and do becomes a leaf, and a buffer that has filled up or aged out is sealed. It fires in minutes because the capture window is lost otherwise.

| # | Stage | What it does | Runs after | Due | Budget |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `leaf_intake` | Admits waiting leaves and appends them to their buffer. | — | continuous | 2 min |
| 2 | `leaf_seal` | Compresses a buffer that crossed its size or age threshold into one seal, and marks its leaves sealed. | `leaf_intake` | continuous | 2 min |
| 3 | `conversation_reflect` | Writes one recap for every conversation that has gone quiet, whichever entry point it arrived through, tagged with that entry point. | `leaf_seal` | continuous | 2 min |

## `consolidate` — 23:00 every day

The night's work: yesterday settled into memory, checked, repaired, and re-indexed — in a declared order, from one start time.

It consumes `leaf_seals` from the other row — declared, so nothing reads across rows by accident.

| # | Stage | What it does | Runs after | Due | Budget |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `agenda_reap` | Abandons the items on the agenda that have sat unfinished past their horizon, so a backlog nobody can finish never crowds out new work. | — | daily | 1 min |
| 2 | `conscience_heartbeat` | Scrapes the day's failures, idle jobs and open breakers into a drift report. | — | daily | 2 min |
| 3 | `daily_writer` | Rolls the day's scheduled runs into the daily log layer. | — | daily | 2 min |
| 4 | `interests_decay` | Ages the interest profile, so one reaction does not weight a topic forever. | — | daily | 1 min |
| 5 | `leaf_digest_daily` | Recomputes one digest across every seal written that day. | — | daily | 5 min |
| 6 | `leaf_topic_route` | Files each seal's sections under the topics its entities earned. | — | daily | 5 min |
| 7 | `vault_raw_watch` | Ingests what you dropped in the vault's raw folder; anything that fails a safety filter is held for you. | — | daily | 15 min |
| 8 | `vault_lint` | Checks the vault wiki for orphans, stale pages, contradictions and missing hubs. | `vault_raw_watch` | daily | 10 min |
| 9 | `work_index_sweep` | Drops index rows pointing at sessions and files that no longer exist. | — | daily | 3 min |
| 10 | `chat_digest` (model) | Reads yesterday's conversations and writes down what mattered. | — | daily | 10 min |
| 11 | `retention` | Ages everything the retention table names — old sessions to the archive, spent logs away, and the permission ledger's old rows to a dated file beside it. | `chat_digest` | daily | 5 min |
| 12 | `feedback_consolidator` (model) | Reviews the whole active feedback set and proposes merges — also as proposals only. | — | weekly | 10 min |
| 13 | `feedback_sweep` (model) | Looks for standing instructions you gave in passing and proposes them; it never writes one itself. | — | daily | 10 min |
| 14 | `librarian_heartbeat` (model) | Consolidates the raw daily layer into canonical memory and refreshes the index. | `chat_digest` | daily | 10 min |
| 15 | `dream_cycle` | Promotes what you keep recalling into longer-lived memory. | `librarian_heartbeat` | daily | 10 min |
| 16 | `memory_lint` | Scans the memory store for broken links, stale paths and empty stubs. | `dream_cycle`, `librarian_heartbeat` | daily | 5 min |
| 17 | `memory_scrub` | Repairs the findings it safely can, and leaves the ones needing your decision. | `memory_lint`\* | daily | 5 min |
| 18 | `index_rebuild` | Rebuilds the keyword and vector indexes over the settled store. | `memory_scrub` | daily | 15 min |
| 19 | `atlas_build` | Redraws the map of how everything you have saved connects — memories, wiki pages, sources and the names in them. | `index_rebuild`, `memory_scrub` | daily | 10 min |
| 20 | `atlas_verify` | Weekly. Redraws the map a second time and checks it matches the one on disk, so the map can never quietly become the thing it describes. | `atlas_build`\* | weekly | 10 min |
| 21 | `memory_relink` (model) | Looks up the memories the map says nothing connects to, and tries to find them relatives. | `atlas_build`\*, `atlas_verify` | daily | 10 min |
| 22 | `provider_probe` (model) | Sends one known-good call to every active role's model, so a dead key or a retired model is found here rather than in the middle of your next request. | — | daily | 10 min |
| 23 | `brief_render` (model) | Writes tomorrow morning's brief, last, so it knows what the night actually did — delivery is a separate service that sends it at the hour you set. | `memory_relink`, `provider_probe`, `retention` | daily | 10 min |

## Order is declared, not timed

A stage names what must run before it, and the runner derives the order above from those names — it is not the order they are written in. Two kinds of edge, and the difference matters when something breaks: a **data** dependency (marked \* in the table) means the stage consumes what the other one produced, so it is skipped when that one did not succeed. A plain ordering edge only places it later; the stage still runs.

That distinction is why an unreachable model cannot cost you the night's maintenance. The deterministic stages commit before anything waits on a provider, and nothing downstream of a model stage is skipped unless it actually reads what that stage writes.

The nightly row's own cadence — `0 23 * * *`, 23:00 every day — is the only clock in the whole arrangement. Move that one line and every stage moves with it, keeping its order.

## Missing a night costs one run, not the work

Each stage remembers how far it got. Come back after a week away and a stage is handed the whole week as one window rather than being run seven times — and the few stages that can only think in single days walk the days they missed, oldest first, bounded so a month away cannot become a month of model calls in one night.

## What a stage reports

Every stage says what came of it, plus how much it changed and how much it declined to touch. There is no state for *ran, produced nothing, called it a win*.

| Outcome | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `succeeded` | It ran and produced something. |
| `skipped_no_work` | It ran and there was nothing to do. Healthy, and it says so rather than reporting a success. |
| `refused` | It deliberately did not start — you turned it off, a breaker was open, or something it needs was missing. |
| `degraded` | It produced less than it promises. A rebuild without embeddings is the usual one. |
| `truncated` | It ran out of its time budget; the rest resumes next run from where it stopped. |
| `failed` | It tried and errored. |
| `skipped_upstream_failed` | Something it consumes did not succeed, so running it would work from stale input. |
